newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish forest industry says "upturn ahead".
newsitem.headline: Finnish forest industry says "upturn ahead".

text.p: The Federation of Finnish Forest Industries said on Wednesday in a report headlined "Upturn ahead" that an increase in European growth is expected but that it is still uncertain.

It said the Finnish forest industry -- very dependent on the overall economic cycle in Europe -- would lose some 7.05 billion markka in export revenue this year due to average production halts of seven to eight weeks.
"Although an (economic) upturn in Western Europe seems to be gradually starting, growth is still on an uncertain base," the federation said.
It said capacity utilisation had increased year-on-year since the levels in late 1995 were already low.

In January-August, the Finnish forest industry's combined profit after financial items fell to four billion markka or seven percent of net sales from nine billion markka or 14 percent of net sales in the year-ago period.
The federation said pulp prices -- a leading price indicator for the sector and particularly for fine papers -- had not risen according to plans due to higher inventories.
"As Norscan stocks have again risen after the summer, the targeted (pulp) price hikes have not been achieved," it said.
"In order for a price rise to materialise, the stocks should fall clearly below 1.5 million tonnes from the current almost 1.8 million tonnes," it said.
But pulp prices were no longer falling and the federation said this was also true for fine papers.
"However, the autumn's hikes have been modest," it added.
"From the beginning of the year, paper prices have fallen by an average of 20 percent," it said.
